rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed about ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy and his companions.
rows.anchor: نزلت في عبد الله بن أبي وأصحابه قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says it concerns hypocrites and some People of the Book who professed faith before the Prophet but contradicted it before their leaders.
rows.anchor: في المنافقين وغيرهم من أهل الكتاب الذين كانوا يظهرون للنبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ilā means maʿa, “with,” as in the verse about helpers “to God.”
rows.anchor: فأما التفسير ف لى بمعنى مع كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One etymology derives shayṭān from shatana, “to be far from good,” making nūn part of the root; Umayya’s shāṭin and al-Nābigha’s shaṭūn attest the sense of distance or rebellion.
rows.anchor: أنه من شطن أي بعد عن الخير فعلى هذا تكون النون أصلية

rows.speaker: أمية بن أبي الصلت
rows.claim: Umayya uses shāṭin of a rebellious being, supporting the derivation from distance from good.
rows.anchor: أيما شاطن عصاه عكاه ثم يلقى في السجن

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nābigha uses shaṭūn for something distant, supporting the same etymology.
rows.anchor: نأت بسعاد عنك نوى شطون فبانت والفؤاد بها رهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second etymology derives shayṭān from shāṭa, “to blaze or burn,” making nūn an added letter.
rows.anchor: أنه من شاط يشيط إذا التهب واحترق فتكون النون زائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse of poetry “وقد يشيط على أرماحنا البطل” uses yashīṭ to mean “perishes,” illustrating the second derivation.
rows.anchor: وقد يشيط على أرماحنا البطل أي يهلك

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud, Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan, and al-Suddi identify their satans as leaders in unbelief.
rows.anchor: انهم رؤوسهم في الكفر قاله ابن مسعود وابن عباس

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya and Mujahid identify their satans as their polytheist brethren.
rows.anchor: إخوانهم من المشركين قاله أبو العالية ومجاهد

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Kalbi identify their satans as their soothsayers.
rows.anchor: كهنتهم قاله الضحاك والكلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We are with you” can mean sharing the same religion or offering support and assistance; huzwa means mockery.
rows.anchor: الثاني إنا معكم على النصرة والمعاضدة والهزء السخرية

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud and Ibn ʿAbbas say the verse was revealed concerning all unbelievers.
rows.anchor: نزلت في جميع الكفار قاله ابن مسعود وابن عباس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada, al-Suddi, and Muqatil say it concerns the People of the Book.
rows.anchor: أنها في أهل الكتاب قاله قتادة والسدي ومقاتل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says it concerns hypocrites.
rows.anchor: أنها في المنافقين قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here “bought” means exchanged: Arabic calls someone who prefers one thing a buyer of it and seller of the other; dalāla and ḍalāl both mean misguidance.
rows.anchor: واشتروا بمعنى استبدلوا والعرب تجعل من آثر شيئا على شئ مشتريا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan, Qatada, and al-Suddi take the exchanged misguidance to mean unbelief and the guidance to mean faith.
rows.anchor: أن المارد هاهنا الكفر والمراد بالهدى الإيمان روي عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation takes misguidance as doubt and guidance as certainty.
rows.anchor: والثاني أنها الشك والهدى اليقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation takes misguidance as ignorance and guidance as knowledge.
rows.anchor: والثالث أنها الجهل والهدى العلم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains the exchange as people who first believed and then disbelieved.
rows.anchor: أنهم آمنوا ثم كفروا قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says the Jews believed in the Prophet before his mission, then disbelieved in him when he was sent.
rows.anchor: أن اليهود آمنوا بالنبي قبل مبعثه فلما بعث كفروا به قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: علي بن عبيد الله
rows.claim: The author’s teacher ʿAli ibn ʿUbayd Allah says those who rejected the Prophet’s guidance effectively traded it for misguidance.
rows.anchor: الضلال كانو كمن أبدل شيئا بشئ ذكره شيخنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Their trade did not profit” is figurative: trade itself does not profit; the trader profits in it. The same construction appears at 34:33 and 47:21, and in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: من مجاز الكلام لأن التجارة لا تربح وإنما يربح فيها

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra, Ibn Qutayba, and al-Zajjaj accept this figurative construction when the intended meaning is clear; it is invalid when a predicate is attached to something that cannot bear it and another meaning is intended.
rows.anchor: و إلى هذا المعنى ذهب الفراء وابن قبية والزجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They were not guided” is explained as lacking knowledge of God.
rows.anchor: وما كانوا في العلم بالله مهتدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that they were not guided out of misguidance.
rows.anchor: وما كانوا مهتدين من الضلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that they were not guided to the believers’ trade.
rows.anchor: وما كانوا مهتدين إلى تجارة المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that they were not guided in their purchase of misguidance.
rows.anchor: وما كانوا مهتدين في اشتراء الضلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fifth explanation says a trader may fail to profit yet remain rightly guided and blameless; denying both profit and guidance intensifies their condemnation.
rows.anchor: قد لا يربح التاجر ويكون على هدى من تجارته غير مستحق للذم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those who break” describes the previously discussed three kinds of transgressors; naqd is the opposite of binding, undoing something after it is secured.
rows.anchor: هذه صفة للفاسقين وقد سبقت فيهم الأقوال الثلاثة والنقض ضد الإبرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Breaking a structure means dismantling what was firmly assembled; breaking a covenant means refusing to abide by its terms.
rows.anchor: فنقض البناء تفريق جمعه بعد إحكامه ونقض العهد الإعراض عن المقام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and Muqatil say the covenant with the People of the Book concerned Muhammad’s description and the command to follow him.
rows.anchor: أنه ما عهد إلى أهل الكتاب من صفة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم والوصية باتباعه قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says it was the covenant they accepted in the Qur’an and then repudiated.
rows.anchor: ما عهد إليهم في القرآن فأقروا به ثم كفروا قاله السدي

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj identifies it as the covenant taken from Adam’s descendants; although unmentioned earlier, the author says a truthful report establishes it and requires belief.
rows.anchor: الذي أخذه عليهم حين استخرج ذرية آدم من ظهره قاله الزجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle min in “after its covenant” is either extra or marks a starting point: the breaking began after the covenant was firmly made.
rows.anchor: أنها زائدة والثاني أنها لابتداء الغاية كأنه قال ابتداء نقض العهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “its covenant” may refer to God or to the covenant, meaning after its firm establishment.
rows.anchor: أنها ترجع إلى الله تعالى والثاني أنها ترجع إلى العهد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, Qatada, and al-Suddi say what God commanded to be joined is kinship and family ties.
rows.anchor: الرحم والقرابة قاله ابن عباس وقتادة والسدي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the command was to maintain connection with the Messenger, which they severed by denying him.
rows.anchor: أنه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قطعوه بالتكذيب قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says it is faith in God without dividing among His messengers; they believed in some and disbelieved in others.
rows.anchor: الإيمان بالله وأن لا يفرق بين أحد من رسله فآمنوا ببعض وكفروا بعض

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says their corruption on earth was calling people to unbelief.
rows.anchor: استدعاؤهم الناس إلى الكفر قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi and Muqatil explain the corruption as committing sins.
rows.anchor: أنه العمل بالمعاصي قاله السدي و مقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation is their intercepting people migrating to the Prophet to prevent conversion to Islam.
rows.anchor: أنه قطعهم الطريق على من جاء مهاجرا إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ليمنعوا الناس من الاسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khusrān means loss or diminution in Arabic.
rows.anchor: والخسران في اللغة لنقصان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and the Medinans read awṣā with alif and a light ṣād, while the other codices/readers have waṣṣā without alif and with doubled ṣād; the author links this to differences between Medinan and Iraqi codices, listing twelve variants.
rows.anchor: قرأ بان عباس وأهل المدينة وأوصى بألف مع تخفيف الصاد والباقون بغير ألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waṣṣā is more emphatic than awṣā because it can indicate repeated acts of counsel.
rows.anchor: ووصى أبلغ من اوصى لأنها تكون لمرات كثيرة

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima and al-Zajjaj say the pronoun in “with it” refers to the matter of counsel.
rows.anchor: وهاء بها تعود على المسألة قاله عكرمة و الزجاج

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil counts Abraham’s sons as four: Ishmael, Isaac, Midian, and Mada'in.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل وبنوه أربعة إسماعيل وإسحاق ومدين ومدائن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other authorities say Abraham’s sons numbered eight.
rows.anchor: وذكر غير مقاتل أنهم ثمانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command not to die except as Muslims means to remain committed to Islam so that death finds one upon it.
rows.anchor: يريد الزموا الإسلام فاذا أدرككم الموت صادفكم عليه

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The verse was revealed after Jews told the Prophet that Jacob had instructed his sons to follow Judaism when he died.
rows.anchor: سبب نزولها أن اليهود قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ألست تعلم أن يعقوب أوصى بنيه يوم مات باليهودية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The buyers chose misguidance over guidance.
rows.anchor: أي اختاروها على الهدى

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima and al-Rabiʿ explain “how patient they are” as patience in deeds that lead them to the Fire.
rows.anchor: فما أصبرهم على عمل يؤديهم إلى النار قاله عكرمة والربيع

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Mujahid take the phrase to mean how bold they are to face the Fire; al-Kisaʾi cites an Arab’s “How bold you are before God!”
rows.anchor: ما أجرأهم على النار قاله الحسن و مجاهد وذكر الكسائي أن أعرابيا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj reads it as asking how long they will remain in the Fire, as in asking how long someone endures imprisonment.
rows.anchor: ما أبقاهم في النار كما تقول ما أصبر فلانا على الحبس

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says it asks what has made them endure the Fire.
rows.anchor: فأي شيء صبرهم على النار قاله ابن الأنباري

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: One grammatical view makes mā interrogative—“what made them patient?”—reported from ʿAta, al-Suddi, Ibn Zayd, and others.
rows.anchor: أنها للاستفهام تقديرها ما الذي أصبرهم قاله عطاء والسدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative makes mā exclamatory, like “how excellent Zayd is”; Ibn al-Anbari says the exclamation is attributed to God to make creatures marvel, not because God marvels as they do.
rows.anchor: أنها للتعجب كقولك ما أحسن زيدا وما أعلم عمرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse explains their behavior by saying God sent the Book in truth and those who differed about it are in deep division.
rows.anchor: ذلك بأن الله نزل الكتاب بالحق وإن الذين اختلفوا في الكتاب

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan explains “by God’s permission” as by God’s help.
rows.anchor: ﴿ بإذن الله ﴾ قال الحسن بنصر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s being with the steadfast means that He grants them victory and assistance.
rows.anchor: ﴿ والله مع الصابرين ﴾ أي بالنصر والاعانة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says dāyantu means transacting with someone by taking a loan from him or lending to him; a cited line about Arwa illustrates settling debts.
rows.anchor: يقال داينت الرجل إذا عاملته فأخذت منه بدين وأعطيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command concerns a debt due at a specified term and requires writing and witnesses to protect property and people from injustice; documented proof restrains a debtor’s temptation to deny it.
rows.anchor: فأمر الله تعالى بكتابة الدين وبالإشهاد حفظا منه للأموال وللناس من الظلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the verse was revealed specifically about salam, an advance-purchase transaction.
rows.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية في السلم خاصة

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari distinguishes tadāyantum for dealing, selling, or lending from dayn for recompense; the latter is pronounced with kasra, as in 51:12, and a cited poem illustrates recompense.
rows.anchor: تداينتم يقع على معنيين أحدهما المشاراة والمبايعة والإقراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿadl means what is right; Qatada says to omit no rightful due and add nothing false.
rows.anchor: فأما العدل فهو الحق قال قتادة لا تدعن حقا ولا تزيدن باطلا

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says a scribe must not refuse to write as God taught him the skill of writing; al-Shaʿbi calls writing a communal duty like jihad.
rows.anchor: كما علمه الله الكتابة قاله سعيد بن جبير وقال الشعبي الكتابة فرض

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj instead understands “as God taught him” to mean writing according to God’s command and truth.
rows.anchor: كما أمره الله به الحق قاله الزجاج

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the person owing the debt must dictate what he owes the claimant to the scribe and must not reduce any part of it.
rows.anchor: يعني المطلوب يقول ليمل ما عليه من حق الطالب على الكاتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amalla and amlā are two forms for dictating; the former is associated with the claimant repeating the statement at length.
rows.anchor: يقال أمللت أمل وأمليت أملي لغتان

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Jubayr define the “foolish” debtor as ignorant about property and unable to dictate.
rows.anchor: الجاهل بالأموال والجاهل بالإملاء قاله مجاهد وابن جبير

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the foolish debtor is a child or a woman.
rows.anchor: أنه الصبي والمرأة قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi identify the foolish debtor as a minor.
rows.anchor: أنه الصغير قاله الضحاك والسدي

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو يعلى
rows.claim: Qadi Abu Yaʿla says foolish here means someone who squanders money.
rows.anchor: أنه المبذر قاله القاضي أبو يعلى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn Jubayr explain “weak” as incapacitated, mute, or mentally unsound.
rows.anchor: أنه العاجر والأخرس ومن به حمق قاله ابن عباس وابن جبير

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid and al-Suddi say “weak” means a fool.
rows.anchor: أنه الأحمق قاله مجاهد والسدي

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو يعلى
rows.claim: Qadi Abu Yaʿla gives “minor” as a third meaning of weak.
rows.anchor: أنه الصغير قاله القاضي أبو يعلى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the debtor cannot dictate because he is slow or tongue-tied; Ibn Jubayr says he cannot properly dictate what he owes, while Qadi Abu Yaʿla says he is insane.
rows.anchor: لا يستطيع لعيه وقال ابن جبير لا يحسن أن يمل ما عليه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn Jubayr, al-Rabiʿ, Muqatil, and Ibn Qutayba say the guardian is the creditor’s guardian, meaning the holder of the right.
rows.anchor: أنها تعود إلى الحق فتقديره فليملل ولي الحق هذا قول ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd say the pronoun refers to the debtor, so his guardian dictates.
rows.anchor: أنها تعود إلى الذي عليه الحق وهذا قول الضحاك وابن زيد

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj prefers the debtor’s guardian: accepting the claimant’s dictation would leave no reason for writing and witnesses, and would simply accept the claimant’s word; Qadi Abu Yaʿla agrees.
rows.anchor: واختاره الزجاج وعاب قول الأولين فقال كيف يقبل قول المدعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿadl means fairness or equity.
rows.anchor: والعدل الإنصاف

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says “your men” means free men.
rows.anchor: أنه يعني الأحرار قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj and Qadi Abu Yaʿla take “your men” to mean Muslims, supported by the verse’s opening address to believers.
rows.anchor: والثاني أهل الإسلام وهذا اختيار الزجاج والقاضي أبي يعلى ويدل عليه أنه خاطب المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “If the two are not men” means if the two witnesses are not both men, not if two men cannot be found.
rows.anchor: أراد فان لم يكن الشهيدان رجلين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says witnesses “whom you approve” are people of merit and religious integrity.
rows.anchor: من أهل الفضل والدين

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the construction means appoint two women so that one may remind the other, or for that purpose.
rows.anchor: معناه استشهدوا امرأتين لأن تذكر إحداهما الأخرى ومن أجل أن تذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza reads in tadhilla with kasra; here dalāl means forgetfulness, according to Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, al-Rabiʿ, Muqatil, and others.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة إن تضل بكسر الألف والضلال هاهنا النسيان قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr read fatudhakkira with a light kaf and accusative ra; Hamza reads it with a doubled kaf and nominative ra; the rest use doubled kaf and accusative ra.
rows.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير و أبو عمرو بالتخفيف مع نصب الراء وقرأ حمزة بالرفع

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: The majority take the light and doubled readings alike: the second woman recalls the matter after the first forgets.
rows.anchor: أنها بمعنى المشددة أيضا وهذا قول الجمهور قال الضحاك والربيع

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna and al-Asmaʿi’s report from Abu ʿAmr take the light reading to make two women’s testimony equivalent to one man’s; Qadi Abu Yaʿla prefers this.
rows.anchor: أنها بمعنى تجعل شهادتهما بمنزلة شهادة ذكر وهذا مذهب سفيان بن عيينة

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli rejects Ibn ʿUyayna’s view: no number of women’s testimony suffices without a man, and forgetfulness should be answered by a reminder.
rows.anchor: ليس مذهب ابن عيينة بالقوي لأنهن لو بلغن ما بلغن لم تجز شاهدتهن

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the verse followed an incident where a man called around a large tented gathering for witnesses and no one came.
rows.anchor: كان الرجل يطوف في الحواء العظيم فيه القوم فيدعوهم إلى الشهادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿAtiyya, Qatada, and al-Rabiʿ say witnesses are called to bear testimony and have it recorded.
rows.anchor: إلى تحمل الشهادة و إثباتها في الكتاب قاله ابن عباس وعطية وقتادة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Tawus, Mujahid, and others say the call is to perform testimony before judges after first bearing it.
rows.anchor: إلى إقامتها وأدائها عند الحكام بعد أن تقدمت شهادتهم بها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A third view, reported from Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Hasan and preferred by al-Zajjaj, includes both bearing and performing testimony.
rows.anchor: والثالث إلى تحملها و إلى أدائها روي عن ابن عباس والحسن واختاره الزجاج

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو يعلى
rows.claim: Qadi Abu Yaʿla says a witness must attend to perform testimony only if no one else can testify; both bearing and performing it are communal duties like jihad.
rows.anchor: إنما يلزم الشاهد أن لا يأبى إذا دعي لإقامة الشهادة إذا لم يوجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not grow weary of recording small or large debts customarily deferred, through their due date; the document is more just, strengthens testimony by reminding witnesses, and more nearly removes doubt.
rows.anchor: أي لا تملوا وتضجروا أن تكتبوا القليل والكثير الذي قد جرت العادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is an immediate exchange in which each party must deliver what it contracted for at once; ʿAsim reads tijāratan in the accusative, treating the funds as the commerce, and writing is waived to avoid burden in ordinary purchases.
rows.anchor: وهي البيوع التي يستحق كل واحد منهما على صاحبه تسليم ما عقد عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witnessing is recommended for transactions where it is customary.
rows.anchor: الإشهاد مندوب إليه فيما جرت العادة بالإشهاد عليه

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority treat writing debts and witnessing sales or debts as recommended, so the command remains operative without abrogation.
rows.anchor: فذهب الجمهور إلى أنه أمر ندب واستحباب فعلى هذا هو محكم

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: A group including Ibn ʿUmar, Abu Musa, Mujahid, Ibn Sirin, and others regard writing and witnessing as obligatory.
rows.anchor: روي عن ابن عمر وابي موسى و مجاهد وابن سيرين وعطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among those who require it, most say the ruling remains, while others say it was abrogated by the trust verse at 2:283.
rows.anchor: فذهب أكثرهم إلى أنه محكم غير منسوخ وذهبت طائفة إلى أنه منسوخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar reads yuḍār with a light ra and sukun.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر بتخفيف الراء من يضار وسكونها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, ʿIkrima, al-Suddi, al-Rabiʿ, al-Farra, and Muqatil say a scribe or witness must not be burdened with a summons while busy; al-Rabiʿ describes a requester insisting despite an available alternative.
rows.anchor: أن معناه لا يضار بأن يدعي وهو مشغول هذا قول ابن عباس و مجاهد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan, Tawus, Qatada, and Ibn Zayd say the scribe must not alter what was dictated, nor the witness testify to something he was not asked to witness; Ibn Qutayba and al-Zajjaj prefer this reading.
rows.anchor: أن معناه النهي للكاتب أن يضار من يكتب له بأن يكتب غير ما يمل عليه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj argues that falsifying a document or testimony is the sort of harm called transgression in the next clause; merely summoning a busy person would not make one sinful.
rows.anchor: واختاره ابن قتيبة و الزجاج واحتج الزجاج على صحته

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: A third view from ʿAta and others says the harm is the scribe refusing to write or the witness refusing to testify.
rows.anchor: أن معنى المضارة امتناع الكاتب أن يكتب والشهادة أن يشهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “If you do so” refers to committing this harm.
rows.anchor: يعني المضارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Travel is singled out because writers and witnesses are less commonly available there; when written documentation is unavailable, take a pledge in hand.
rows.anchor: إنما خص السفر لأن الأغلب عدم الكاتب والشاهد فيه ومقصود الكلام

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʿAmr, and ʿAbd al-Warith read ruhun without alif; ʿAbd al-Warith also has a sukun for ease of pronunciation.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعبد الوارث فرهن بضم الراء والهاء من غير ألف

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nafiʿ, ʿAsim, Ibn ʿAmir, Hamza, and al-Kisaʾi read rihān with alif; Ibn Qutayba says this is a plural of rahn, whereas ruhun is a plural of rihān.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزه والكسائي ﴿ فرهان ﴾ بكسر الراء وفتح الهاء

rows.speaker: أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن
rows.claim: Abu Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman says the verse was revealed about waiting for one prayer after another, at a time without a campaign requiring frontier watch.
rows.anchor: نزلت في انتظار الصلاة بعد الصلاة وليس يؤمئذ غزو يرابط

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Patience is variously explained as enduring trials and jihad (Ibn ʿAbbas), religion (al-Hasan, al-Qurazi, al-Zajjaj), afflictions (al-Hasan), obligations (Saʿid ibn Jubayr), or obedience to God (Qatada).
rows.anchor: البلاء والجهاد قاله ابن عباس الثاني الدين قاله الحسن والقرظي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The command to outlast others is explained as steadfastness against the enemy by Ibn ʿAbbas and most authorities, or steadfastness in God’s promise by ʿAta and al-Qurazi.
rows.anchor: العدو قاله ابن عباس والجمهور والثاني الوعد الذي وعدهم الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Frontier ribat means preparing horses against the enemy, with each side readying its horses, as Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan, Qatada, and others say.
rows.anchor: الجهاد للأعداء قاله ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة في آخرين

rows.speaker: أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن
rows.claim: Abu Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman gives an alternative: maintaining vigilance in prayer.
rows.anchor: أنه الصلاة أمروا بالمرابطة عليها قاله أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The verse followed Rifaʿa’s death, when his young son Thabit’s guardian uncle asked the Prophet what he could take from the orphan’s property and when to hand it over.
rows.anchor: أن رجلا يقال له رفاعة مات وترك ولدا صغيرا يقال له ثابت فوليه عمه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The orphan’s trial is to test his judgment, according to Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Suddi, Sufyan, and Muqatil.
rows.anchor: أنهم يختبرون في عقولهم قاله ابن عباس والسدي وسفيان ومقاتل

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada say the trial tests both reason and religion; Mujahid is reported with either this or the reason-only view.
rows.anchor: يختبرون في عقولهم ودينهم قاله الحسن وقتادة وعن مجاهد

rows.speaker: الثعلبي
rows.claim: Al-Thaʿlabi adds that the test concerns reason, religion, and safeguarding property; Qadi Abu Yaʿla says it occurs before puberty.
rows.anchor: في عقولهم ودينهم وحفظهم أموالهم ذكره الثعلبي

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba explains “reach marriage” as becoming old enough to marry women; ānastum means you know or discern, originally “saw.”
rows.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة أي بلغوا أن ينكحوا النساء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Rushd is soundness in religion and care of property according to Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Hasan.
rows.anchor: الصلاح في الدين وحفظ المال قاله ابن عباس والحسن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Suddi defines it as sound judgment and care of property.
rows.anchor: الصلاح في العقل وحفظ المال روي عن ابن عباس والسدي

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid and al-Nakhaʿi define maturity as reason.
rows.anchor: أنه العقل قاله مجاهد والنخعي

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: A report from al-Suddi combines reason and religious soundness.
rows.anchor: العقل والصلاح في الدين روي عن السدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Removal of an orphan’s legal restraint depends on both puberty and maturity; guardians must test them and deliver their property once maturity is clear.
rows.anchor: علق رفع الحجر عن اليتامى بأمرين بالبلوغ والرشد وأمر الأولياء باختبارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Puberty has five indicators: wet dream, age fifteen, or pubic hair for either sex, and menstruation or pregnancy for women.
rows.anchor: الاحتلام واستكمال خمس عشرة سنة والإنبات وشيئان يختصان بالنساء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The prohibition addresses guardians: Ibn ʿAbbas says not to consume an orphan’s property without right, or hasten to consume it before the child grows up.
rows.anchor: خطاب للأولياء قال ابن عباس لا تأكلوها بغير حق وبدارا تبادرون أكل المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wealthy guardian should refrain from using the orphan’s assets and live on his own wealth.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ومن كان غنيا فليستعفف ﴾ بماله عن مال اليتيم

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: One view allows a poor guardian to take an advance loan, reported from ʿUmar, Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn Jubayr, and others.
rows.anchor: أنه الأخذ على وجه القرض وهذا مروي عن عمر وابن عباس وابن جبير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another view permits only enough for the guardian’s needs, without excess; it is reported from Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan, ʿIkrima, and others.
rows.anchor: الأكل بمقدار الحاجة من غير إسراف وهذا مروي عن ابن عباس والحسن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A third view lets the guardian take a customary wage for work done for the orphan, reported from Ibn ʿAbbas and ʿAʾisha.
rows.anchor: أنه الأخذ بقدر الأجرة إذا عمل لليتيم عملا روي عن ابن عباس وعائشة

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbi allows taking only when necessary, with repayment if the guardian later becomes solvent and no repayment if he does not.
rows.anchor: أنه الأخذ عند الضرورة فان أيسر قضاه وإن لم يوسر فهو في حل

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: The majority treat the allowance as operative: the wealthy may take nothing, while a poor guardian occupied with the orphan’s care may take enough by custom without excess.
rows.anchor: حكمها عندهم أن الغني ليس له أن يأكل من مال اليتيم شيئا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Some authorities say a guardian who later becomes solvent need not repay, since the amount is compensation for his service.
rows.anchor: أنه لا ضمان عليه بل يكون كالأجرة له على عمله وهو قول الحسن

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Others say repayment becomes due if the guardian later becomes solvent; Ibn ʿAbbas is reported on both sides.
rows.anchor: إذا أيسر وجب عليه القضاء روي عن عمر وغيره وعن ابن عباس أيضا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A minority says the permission was abrogated by 4:29, but the author says this report from Ibn ʿAbbas is unsound.
rows.anchor: وهذا مروي عن ابن عباس ولا يصح

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو يعلى
rows.claim: Witnesses at delivery are a precaution, not an obligation; evidence protects the orphan from falsely denying receipt and the guardian from an oath if delivery is disputed.
rows.anchor: هذا على طريق الاحتياط لليتيم والولي وليس بواجب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Suddi, and Muqatil say hasīb means witness.
rows.anchor: أنه الشهيد قاله ابن عباس والسدي ومقاتل

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba and al-Khattabi say hasīb means sufficient or enough, deriving it from “this sufficed me.”
rows.anchor: أنه الكافي من قولك أحسبني هذا الشيء أي كفاني

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba and al-Khattabi also explain hasīb as reckoner/accountant, on the pattern of words for table-companion and drinker.
rows.anchor: أنه المحاسب فيكون في مذهب جليس وأكيل وشريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are called losers because they exchanged faith for unbelief; meeting God means resurrection and recompense, the Hour is the Resurrection, and baghta means suddenly, as al-Zajjaj’s poetry illustrates.
rows.anchor: لأنهم باعوا الإيمان بالكفر فعظم خسرانهم والمراد بلقاء الله البعث والجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hasra is grief over something lost; exegetes gloss the cry as “our regret.”
rows.anchor: الحسرة التلهف على الشيء الفائت وأهل التفسير يقولون يا ندامتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling out to an inanimate regret is an Arabic device for forceful emphasis: the intended audience is onlookers, not regret itself; parallels include “O horses of God, ride,” as Sibawayh explains.
rows.anchor: إذا اجتهدت في المبالغة في الإخبار عن عظيم ما تقع فيه جعلته نداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafriṭ means wasting or neglecting; al-Zajjaj also glosses it as delay caused by incapacity.
rows.anchor: فأما التفريط فهو التضييع وقال الزجاج التفريط في اللغة تقدمه العجز

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The pronoun in “in it” may refer to this worldly life, meaning they neglected afterlife deeds there, according to Muqatil.
rows.anchor: أنها الدنيا فالمعنى على ما ضيعنا في الدنيا من عمل الآخرة قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir says the pronoun refers to an unstated transaction, since loss only occurs in a transaction and the context makes it understood.
rows.anchor: أنها الصفقة لأن الخسران لا يكون إلا في صفقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some exegetes take the pronoun to refer to obedience.
rows.anchor: والثالث أنها الطاعة ذكره بعض المفسرين

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba says awzār are sins, with the root sense of a load on the back; Ibn Faris likewise defines wizr as weight.
rows.anchor: هي الآثام واصل الوزر الحمل على الظهر وقال ابن فارس الوزر الثقل

rows.speaker: عمير بن هانئ
rows.claim: One view takes the carrying literally: ʿUmayr ibn Haniʾ describes each unbeliever’s deed appearing as an ugly man that mounts him and exposes him publicly; al-Suddi, ʿAmr ibn Qays, and Muqatil also hold this view.
rows.anchor: يحشر مع كل كافر عمله في صورة رجل قبيح كلما كان هول عظمه عليه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says carrying the burdens is figurative: the weight of their sins, with punishment treated as the heaviest thing they could bear.
rows.anchor: أنه مثل والمعنى يحملون ثقل ذنوبهم قاله الزجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “How evil is what they carry” means how vile a burden they bear.
rows.anchor: بئس الشيء شيئا يزرونه أي يحملونه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Abraham’s people argued with him about their gods and threatened him through them.
rows.anchor: جادلوه في آلهتهم وخوفوه بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʿAmr, Hamza, and al-Kisaʾi double the nūn in atuḥājjūnī and taʾmurūnī; Nafiʿ and Ibn ʿAmir lighten it by dropping the second nūn where the two meet.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Do you argue with me about God?” means about His oneness; “He guided me” means He showed him the way of guidance.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أتحاجوني في الله ﴾ أي في توحيده

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi reads hadān with imāla of the dāl, appropriate to a verb whose root contains yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي هداني بإمالة الدال والإمالة حسنة فيما كان أصله الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham does not fear the idols because they can neither harm nor benefit; he fears only what his Lord wills, whose knowledge encompasses everything fully.
rows.anchor: لا أخافها لأنها لا تضر ولا تنفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols cannot harm or benefit, while the polytheists should fear the God who created and sustains them and can harm or benefit them.
rows.anchor: من هذه الأصنام التي لا تضر ولا تنفع ولا تخافون أنتم أنكم أشركتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Authority” means a proof God sent down for the partners they claim.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ما لم ينزل به عليكم سلطانا ﴾ أي حجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks which group is safer from punishment: the monotheist worshipping the source of harm and benefit, or the polytheist worshipping what can neither harm nor benefit.
rows.anchor: الموحد الذي يعبد من بيده الضر والنفع أم المشرك الذي يعبد مالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not mixing faith with wrongdoing means not mixing it with shirk; an authentic report from Ibn Masʿud says Muslims worried until the Prophet identified the wrongdoing as shirk and cited 31:13.
rows.anchor: أي يخلطوه بشرك روى البخاري ومسلم في صحيحيهما من حديث ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: One view, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, says the verse refers to Abraham and his companions, with another report limiting it to Abraham alone, not this community.
rows.anchor: أنه إبراهيم وأصحابه وليست في هذه الأمة قاله علي بن أبي طالب

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima says it refers to those who migrated to Medina.
rows.anchor: أنه من هاجر إلى المدينة قاله عكرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view makes the verse general to all believers.
rows.anchor: والثالث أنها عامة ذكره بعض المفسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes also differ on whether this statement is Abraham’s words to his people or God’s response.
rows.anchor: وهل هي من قول إبراهيم لقومه أم جواب من الله تعالى فيه قولان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā means “that which.” The particle lā may be extra; if it is negative, the clause can mean “I recite to you the prohibition of associating partners.”
rows.anchor: ما بمعنى الذي وفي لا قولان أحدهما أنها زائدة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj gives another construal: “I advise you not to associate partners,” with the following command about parents understood as part of the same advice.
rows.anchor: أن يكون المعنى أوصيكم أن لا تشركوا لأن قوله

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: If the sentence ends at “what your Lord prohibited,” Ibn al-Anbari takes ʿalaykum as an admonition: you must not associate partners.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أنها إغراء كقوله ﴿ عليكم أنفسكم ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative construal takes ʿalaykum to mean that it is imposed and made obligatory upon you.
rows.anchor: أن يكون بمعنى فرض عليكم ووجب عليكم أن لا تشركوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shirk here is either claiming that God has a partner or obeying another in disobedience to God.
rows.anchor: أنه ادعاء شريك مع الله عز وجل والثاني أنه طاعة غيره في معصيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ban on killing children refers to burying daughters alive; imlāq means fear of poverty.
rows.anchor: يريد دفن البنات أحياء ﴿ من إملاق ﴾ أي من خوف فقر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan, and al-Suddi take the manifest and hidden indecencies as adultery done openly or secretly.
rows.anchor: الزنا وما ظهر منه الإعلان به وما بطن الاستسرار به قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr and Mujahid say outward indecencies are wine and forbidden marriages, while hidden indecency is adultery.
rows.anchor: ما ظهر الخمر ونكاح المحرمات وما بطن الزنا قاله سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the outward indecency is wine and the hidden one adultery.
rows.anchor: ما ظهر الخمر وما بطن الزنا قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada takes the wording generally: indecencies publicly displayed and privately concealed.
rows.anchor: أنه عام في الفواحش وظاهرها علانيتها وباطنها سرها قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi says outward indecencies are bodily acts and hidden ones are beliefs of the heart, paralleling 7:33.
rows.anchor: ما ظهر أفعال الجوارح وما بطن اعتقاد القلوب ذكره الماوردي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The protected life is that of a Muslim or a person under treaty; killing is permitted only by authorization of religious law.
rows.anchor: والنفس التي حرم الله نفس مسلم أو معاهد والمراد بالحق إذن الشرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An orphan’s property is singled out because weak oversight and the owner’s vulnerability make it especially tempting to seize.
rows.anchor: إنما خص مال اليتيم لأن الطمع فيه لقلة مراعيه وضعف مالكه أقوى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One interpretation permits a guardian to consume customary amounts while in need, according to Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn Zayd.
rows.anchor: أنه أكل الوصي المصلح للمال بالمعروف وقت حاجته قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi interpret the best manner as trading with the orphan’s property.
rows.anchor: التجارة فيه قاله سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد والضحاك والسدي

rows.speaker: ابن السائب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Saʾib says it means preserving the property until it is delivered to the orphan.
rows.anchor: أنه حفظه له إلى وقت تسليمه إليه قاله ابن السائب

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says to preserve and grow the property; “until maturity” implies keeping it safe until then and handing it over afterward.
rows.anchor: أنه حفظه عليه وتثميره له قاله الزجاج

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba defines ashudd as the full strength of youth before decline; the term has several proposed singular forms, or no singular at all.
rows.anchor: فأما الأشد فهو استحكام قوة الشباب والسن قال ابن قتيبة

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr transmits from Ibn ʿAbbas that ashudd is thirty-three years.
rows.anchor: أنه ثلاث وثلاثون سنة رواه ابن جبير عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: Abu Salih transmits from Ibn ʿAbbas that ashudd is between eighteen and thirty years.
rows.anchor: ما بين ثماني عشرة إلى ثلاثين سنة قاله أبو صالح عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: A report from ʿAʾisha identifies ashudd as forty years.
rows.anchor: أربعون سنة روي عن عائشة عليها السلام

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr and Muqatil say ashudd is eighteen years.
rows.anchor: ثماني عشرة سنة قاله سعيد بن جبير ومقاتل

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima gives twenty-five years as the age of ashudd.
rows.anchor: خمس وعشرون سنة قاله عكرمة

rows.speaker: سفيان الثوري
rows.claim: Sufyan al-Thawri gives thirty-four years as the age of ashudd.
rows.anchor: أربع وثلاثون سنة قاله سفيان الثوري

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi gives thirty years and suggests that the later marriage-age verse may have abrogated this ruling.
rows.anchor: ثلاثون سنة قاله السدي وقال ثم جاء بعد هذه الآية

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: The author says the correct meaning of ashudd is puberty, as Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Shaʿbi, Yahya ibn Yaʿmar, Rabiʿa, and Malik hold.
rows.anchor: والثامن بلوغ الحلم قاله زيد بن أسلم والشعبي ويحيى بن يعمر وربيعة ومالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author doubts the earlier age reports belong here, suspecting compilers transferred them from the interpretation of 12:22; he distinguishes reaching full growth from its completion.
rows.anchor: ولا أظن بالذين حكينا عنهم الأقوال التي قبله فسروا هذه الآية بما ذكر عنهم

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir supplies an ellipsis: protect the orphan’s property until maturity, then, once maturity and good judgment are found, deliver it.
rows.anchor: حتى يبلغ أشده فإذا بلغ أشده فآنستم منه رشدا فادفعوا إليه ماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the claim that all this is already explicit in the verse: maturity and Islam are drawn from another verse, so an unqualified statement is limited by the qualified one.
rows.anchor: فليس بصحيح وإنما استفيد إيناس الرشد والإسلام من آية أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fulfill the measure and do not reduce it; qist means justice. A person is charged only within capacity.
rows.anchor: والقسط العدل ﴿ لا نكلف نفسا إلا وسعها ﴾ أي ما يسعها ولا تضيق عنه

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو يعلى
rows.claim: Qadi Abu Yaʿla says exact infinitesimal precision is impossible in weighing and measuring, so one must strive carefully rather than guarantee perfection.
rows.anchor: يتعذر فيهما التحديد بأقل القليل كلفنا الاجتهاد في التحري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speak or testify justly, telling the truth even when the person concerned is a relative; God’s covenant includes His commands and vows people impose on themselves.
rows.anchor: إذا تكلمتم أو شهدتم فقولوا الحق ولو كان المشهود له أو عليه ذا قرابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose of these instructions is that people remember and act on them.
rows.anchor: وعهد الله يشتمل على ما عهده إلى الخلق وأوصاهم به وعلى ما أوجبه الإنسان على نفسه

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr read the listed forms of tadhakkur with a doubled dhāl.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو تذكرون ويذكرون ويذكر الإنسان

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nafiʿ, Abu Bakr from ʿAsim, and Ibn ʿAmir double the dhāl in all these forms except “does the human not remember,” which they lighten.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وأبو بكر عن عاصم وابن عامر كل ذلك بالتشديد إلا قوله

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Aban and Hafs from ʿAsim read yadhkurun with a light dhāl throughout; Hamza and al-Kisaʾi double it with yāʾ but lighten it with tāʾ.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي يذكرون مشددا إذا كان بالياء ومخففا إذا كان بالتاء

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafiʿ, ʿAsim, and Abu ʿAmr read wa-anna with fatḥa and doubled nūn; al-Farra allows it to depend on “I recite” or on “that is what He enjoined, and that this is My path.”
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم وأبو عمرو وأن بفتح الألف مع تشديد النون

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAmir reads the particle with fatḥa but a light nūn, treating it as a reduced form of the emphatic particle.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر بفتح الألف أيضا إلا أنه خفف النون

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read the particle with kasra and doubled nūn as the start of a new sentence.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي بتشديد النون مع كسر الألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is interpreted as either the Qurʾan or Islam.
rows.anchor: وفي الصراط قولان أحدهما أنه القرآن والثاني الإسلام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the paths are misguidances; Mujahid says innovations and doubts; Muqatil says forbidden livestock and crops.
rows.anchor: السبل فقال ابن عباس هي الضلالات وقال مجاهد البدع والشبهات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following other paths diverts people from God’s path, meaning His religion.
rows.anchor: فتضلكم عن دينه

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: The sorcerers prostrated by choice, but the clear miracle removed every doubt and impelled them to hurry into prostration; the passive “were cast” magnifies what they witnessed.
rows.anchor: زالت كل شبهة بما أظهر الله تعالى من أمره اضطرهم عظيم ما عاينوا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says that after the sorcerers believed, six hundred thousand Israelites followed Moses.
rows.anchor: لما آمنت السحرة اتبع موسى ستمائة ألف من بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Crosswise” means the right hand and left leg are cut off.
rows.anchor: وهو قطع اليد اليمنى والرجل اليسر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Pharaoh was the first to carry out cross-amputation and the first to crucify.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس أول من فعل ذلك وأول من صلب فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sorcerers tell Pharaoh he resents nothing in them except that they believed.
rows.anchor: وما تكره منا شيئا ولا تعطن علينا إلا لأنا آمنا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says their prayer for patience asks for endurance through amputation and crucifixion so they will not revert to unbelief.
rows.anchor: على القطع والصلب حتى لا نرجع كفارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their request to die as Muslims means to remain sincere upon Moses’ religion.
rows.anchor: أي مخلصين على دين موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a polytheist under a death order requests protection to hear the Qurʾan and consider its commands and prohibitions, grant refuge and then escort him to safety.
rows.anchor: استأمنك يبتغي أن يسمع القرآن وينظر فيما أمر به ونهي عنه فأجره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They are a people who do not know” may explain why they are to be taught and protected: they lack knowledge.
rows.anchor: ذلك الذي أمرناك به من أن يعرفوا ويجاروا لجهلهم بالعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase explains why a non-convert must be escorted back to safety: the people are ignorant of God’s command.
rows.anchor: من رده إلى مأمنه إذا امتنع من الإيمان لأنهم قوم جهلة بخطاب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God provides rain from heaven and plants from earth; He created hearing and sight and brings the living from the dead and the dead from the living, as previously discussed at 3:27.
rows.anchor: المطر ومن الأرض النبات ( أم من يملك السمع ) أي خلق السمع والأبصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God directs the affairs of this world and the next; the audience admits it is God because only He can do these things, proving His oneness.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى ( ومن يدبر الأمر ) أي أمر الدنيا والآخرة ( فسيقولون الله ) لأنهم خوطبوا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas interprets “will you not be mindful?” as “will you not take warning?”
rows.anchor: أفلا تتعظون قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil reads the question as “will you not fear associating partners with God?”
rows.anchor: تتقون الشرك قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: الخطابي
rows.claim: Al-Khattabi defines the Real as that whose existence is established and valid.
rows.anchor: الحق هو المتحقق وجوده وكل شيء صح وجوده وكونه فهو حق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains “how are you turned away?” as asking how reason can turn people toward worshipping what neither provides, gives life, nor causes death.
rows.anchor: كيف تصرف عقولكم إلى عبادة من لا يرزق ولا يحيى ولا يميت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “those who bar others from God’s path” was explained earlier at 7:45.
rows.anchor: قد تقدم تفسيرها في ( الأعراف 45 )

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the second “they” in “they are disbelievers in the Hereafter” emphasizes the gravity of their disbelief.
rows.anchor: ذكرت هم ثانية على جهة التوكيد لشأنهم في الكفر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The first interpretation takes “they could not hear” as the unbelievers being prevented by God from hearing good, seeing truth, and performing obedience; Ibn ʿAbbas and Muqatil are associated with this reading.
rows.anchor: لم يقدروا على استماع الخير وإبصار الحق وفعل الطاعة لأن الله تعالى حال

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra offers another reading: their punishment is multiplied because they could hear and see God’s proofs but ignored and failed to heed them; the causal preposition is omitted, as in the cited Arabic verse.
rows.anchor: بما كانوا يستطيعون السمع ولا يسمعونه وبما كانوا يبصورن حجج الله

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says their intense unbelief and hostility to the Prophet made them unable to understand what he said.
rows.anchor: من شدة كفرهم وعداوتهم للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ما كانوا يستطيعون أن يتفهموا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A second interpretation makes the referent the idols: they lacked hearing and sight and therefore could not hear or see; this interpretation is also transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbas.
rows.anchor: أنهم الأصنام فالمعنى ما كان للآلهة سمع ولا بصر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says lā jarama means “truly.”
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس يريد حقا إنهم الأخسرون

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says lā jarama originally meant “there is no escape or doubt,” then frequent use made it equivalent to “truly”; its root is jarama, to earn sin.
rows.anchor: كانت في الأصل بمنزلة لا بد ولا محالة فجرت على ذلك

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj construes lā as denying benefit: their deeds do not benefit them; rather, they earned loss in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج ومعنى لا جرم لا نفي لما ظنوا أنه ينفعهم كأن المعنى لا ينفعهم ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says lā answers unbelievers who think punishment will be diverted, then jarama begins a new clause; jarama either means their unbelief earned punishment or that punishment was made sure, with a poem supporting the latter.
rows.anchor: لا رد على أهل الكفر فيما قدروه من اندفاع الشر عنهم في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The various dialect forms—lā jarama, lā jarama without mīm, lā dhā jarama, and related forms—all mean “certainly.”
rows.anchor: ومعنى اللغات كلها حقا

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra, al-Hasan, Ibn al-Sumayfiʿ, and al-Aʿmash read ʿishāʾ with a ḍamma on the first letter.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو هريرة والحسن وابن السميفع والأعمش عشاء بضم العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They came at nightfall because darkness made them bolder in presenting their fabricated excuse.
rows.anchor: جاؤوا وقت العتمة ليكونوا أجرأ في الظلمة على الاعتذار بالكذب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn Qutayba explain nastabiq as competing in archery.
rows.anchor: ننتضل قاله ابن عباس وابن قتيبة قال والمعنى يسابق بعضنا بعضا في الرمي

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the brothers went out racing on foot.
rows.anchor: نشتد قاله السدي

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says they went hunting.
rows.anchor: نتصيد قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Matāʿ means their clothes; muʾmin means one who believes their claim.
rows.anchor: أي ثيابنا ( وما أنت بمؤمن لنا ) أي يمصدق

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq takes “even if we were truthful” to mean even if what they said were true.
rows.anchor: أن المعنى وإن كنا قد صدقنا قاله ابن إسحاق

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says that even if they were normally trustworthy, Jacob would still suspect them about Joseph because he loved him and think they had lied.
rows.anchor: لو كنا عندك من أهل الصدق لا تهمتنا في يوسف لمحبتك

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: “False blood” means blood in which a lie was made: Arabic often uses a verbal noun in the passive-object sense, as in maʿqūl for reason and majlūd for skin; al-Farra, al-Akhfash, al-Zajjaj, and Ibn Qutayba explain the usage, with poetry as evidence.
rows.anchor: معناه بدم مكذوب فيه والعرب تجعل المصدر في كثير من الكلام مفعولا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says they killed a young goat and dipped Joseph’s shirt in its blood; Jacob noticed the shirt was untorn and said a wolf would have torn it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس أخذوا جديا فذبحوه ثم غمسوا قميص يوسف في دمه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the blood on the shirt was from a gazelle.
rows.anchor: كان دم ظبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Abi ʿAbla reads kadhaban in the accusative; Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan, and Abu al-ʿAliya read kadhb with an unpointed dhal, meaning fresh blood.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة بدم كذبا بالنصب وقرأ ابن عباس والحسن

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and ʿIkrima read “from all you asked” literally as all the things you requested.
rows.anchor: أن المعنى من كل الذي سألتموه قاله الحسن وعكرمة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says it means everything you would ask for, even hypothetically.
rows.anchor: من كل ما سألتموه لو سألتوه قاله الفراء

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash supplies an omitted “something”: God gave you something of everything you asked for, as in 27:23.
rows.anchor: وآتاكم من كل شيء سألتموه شيئا فأضمر الشيء

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says the wording also includes blessings not requested—such as the sun and moon—by mentioning what was asked and letting it imply what was not, as at 16:81.
rows.anchor: وما لم تسألوه لأنكم لم تسألوا شمسا ولا قمرا ولا كثيرا من النعم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: On a reading with tanwin and no possessive construction, Qatada and al-Dahhak say the phrase means God gave you what you did not ask for.
rows.anchor: من كل ما بالتنوين من غير إضافة فالمعنى آتاكم من كل ما لم تسألوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Niʿmat Allah means God’s benefaction, too abundant for anyone to enumerate exhaustively.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ وإن تعدوا نعمة الله ﴾ أي إنعامه ﴿ لا تحصوها ﴾ لا تطيقوا الإتيان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas identifies “the human” as Abu Jahl.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس يريد أبا جهل

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says “the human” is grammatically the species but refers specifically to the unbeliever.
rows.anchor: الإنسان اسم للجنس يقصد به الكافر خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ẓalūm means one who wrongs by failing to thank the benefactor; kaffār means one who denies God’s blessings.
rows.anchor: الظلوم هاهنا الشاكر غير من أنعم عليه والكفار الجحود لنعم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable of worldly life concerns how quickly it runs out, or how its changing fortunes pair every joy with grief; the comparison is elaborated at 10:24.
rows.anchor: في سرعة نفادها وذهابها وقيل في تصرف احوالها إذ مع كل فرحة ترحة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra defines hasīm as anything that was moist and dried; al-Zajjaj calls it dry vegetation, while Ibn Qutayba describes brittle, crumbling plants and derives the word from breaking.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء الهشيم كل شيء كان رطبا فيبس وقال الزجاج الهشيم النبات الجاف

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy, Ibn ʿAbbas, and Ibn Abi ʿAbla read tadhrihi with a raised tāʾ and a kasra on rāʾ followed by silent yāʾ and hāʾ; Ibn Masʿud has the same except fatḥa on tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي وابن عباس وابن أبي عبلة تذريه برفع التاء وكسر الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqtadir is on the iftaʿala pattern from q-d-r; commentators say God can create and annihilate anything.
rows.anchor: والمقتدر مفتعل من قدرت قال المفسرون وكان الله على كل شيء من الإنشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth and children answer the pagans’ pride: they adorn worldly life but do not benefit people in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: هذا رد على المشركين الذين كانوا يفتخرون بالأموال والأولاد

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: One view identifies lasting good deeds as saying Subḥān Allah, al-ḥamdu lillāh, lā ilāha illa Allah, and Allahu akbar; Abu Hurayra transmits a Prophetic report urging these words when night worship or fighting is beyond one’s ability.
rows.anchor: روى أبو هريرة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال إن عجزتم عن الليل

rows.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
rows.claim: ʿUthman ibn ʿAffan gives the same formula and adds lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā bi-llāh; Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib and Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi agree.
rows.anchor: وسئل عثمان ابن عفان رضي الله عنه عن الباقيات الصالحات فقال هذه الكلمات

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: A report from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib from the Prophet gives the formula as lā ilāha illa Allah, Allahu akbar, al-ḥamdu lillāh, and lā quwwata illa bi-llāh.
rows.anchor: أنها لا إله إلا الله والله اكبر والحمد لله ولا قوة الا بالله رواه علي

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr transmits from Ibn ʿAbbas that the lasting good deeds are the five prayers; Ibn Masʿud, Masruq, and Ibrahim share this view.
rows.anchor: أنها الصلوات الخمس رواه سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: العوفي
rows.claim: Al-ʿAwfi transmits from Ibn ʿAbbas that the lasting good deeds are good words.
rows.anchor: الكلام الطيب رواه العوفي عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن أبي طلحة
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Talha transmits from Ibn ʿAbbas that the term covers all good deeds; Qatada and Ibn Zayd agree.
rows.anchor: هي جميع أعمال الحسنات وراه ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are better in reward and a better hope than worldly expectations, which may fail, whereas this hope does not.
rows.anchor: لأن آمالكم كواذب وهذا أمل لا يكذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They denied the signs of God’s oneness and denied resurrection and recompense; their rejection of the Messenger and Qurʾan entails those denials, so their efforts are void for lack of faith.
rows.anchor: جحدوا دلائل توحيده وكفروا بالبعث والجزاء وذلك أنهم بكفرهم برسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud and al-Jahdari read “we do not establish” with a masculine yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود والجحدري فلا يقيم بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation says only obedience weighs in the balance, and an unbeliever has no obedience to weigh.
rows.anchor: إنما يثقل الميزان بالطاعة وإنما توزن الحسنات والسيئات والكافر لا طاعة له

rows.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrabi says “no weight” means no worth or rank; a Prophetic report from Abu Hurayra says a tall, gluttonous drinker will not weigh a mosquito’s wing.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأعرابي في تفسير هذه الآية يقال ما لفلان عندنا وزن

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari gives a third interpretation: the scales are not established in their favor, because they weigh against them.
rows.anchor: فلا نقيم لهم لأن الوزن عليهم لا لهم ذكره ابن الأنباري

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih reports that Moses asked Shuʿayb to return to his mother, then left with his family; on a cold night a child was born, his fire-starting failed, and he saw fire to the left of the road.
rows.anchor: قال وهب بن منبه استأذن موسى شعيبا عليهما السلام في الرجوع إلى والدته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commentators say Moses saw a light, but the account reports his assumption that it was a fire; he told his wife to wait where she was.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون رأى نورا ولكن اخبر بما كان في ظن موسى فقال لأهله يعنى امرأته

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza reads the hāʾ in li-ahlihi with ḍamma here and in the parallel phrasing.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة لأهله امكثوا بضم الهاء ها هنا

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says ānastu means “I found”; Ibn Qutayba says it means “I saw.”
rows.anchor: قال الفراء اني وجدت يقال هل آنست احدا اي وجدت

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines a qabas as fire taken at the end of a stick or wick.
rows.anchor: هو ما أخذته من النار في رأس عود أو في رأس فتيلة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says Moses meant “a guide,” using the verbal noun form huda for a guide.
rows.anchor: أراد هاديا فذكره بلفظ المصدر

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says ʿalā here can mean “at,” “with,” or “by.”
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأنبارى يجوز ان تكون ﴿ على ﴾ ها هنا بمعنى ﴿ عند ﴾ وبمعنى مع وبمعنى الباء

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Commentators say Moses had lost the road; al-Zajjaj adds that he had lost the water and hoped to find someone to guide him to the road or water.
rows.anchor: ضل عن الماء فرجا أن يجد من يهديه الطريق أو يدله على الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their repeated cry was “Woe to us, we were wrongdoers”; they continued saying it until punishment made them like harvested crop, or swords did so, and they became still as extinguished fire.
rows.anchor: ما زالت تلك الكلمة التي هي يا ويلنا إنا كنا ظالمين قولهم يرددونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Rather” dismisses their false claim: God casts the Qurʾanic truth upon their lie and crushes it; Ibn Qutayba derives the image from a lethal blow to the brain, and the falsehood vanishes.
rows.anchor: نقذف بالحق أي نسلط الحق وهو القرآن على الباطل وهو كذبهم فيدمغه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commentators explain that God invalidates their falsehood with the truth until it disappears; woe is due for describing God with what is improper.
rows.anchor: إنا نبطل كذبهم بما نثبين من الحق حتى يضمحل ولكم الويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apostate worships what neither harms him if he does not worship it nor benefits him if he obeys it; this is remote misguidance, far from the truth.
rows.anchor: هذا المرتد أي يعبد مالا يضره إن لم يعبده ولا ينفعه إن أطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment raining down on them consisted of stones.
rows.anchor: يعني الحجارة

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
rows.claim: Muqatil ibn Sulayman says Shuʿayb is not called the “brother” of the people of the Thicket because he was not descended from them; he was sent to them after Midian, whose lineage he shared.
rows.anchor: أن شعيبا لم يكن من نسل أصحاب الأيكة فلذلك لم يقل أخوهم

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi says Midian was punished by the canopy; if Midian differed from the Thicket people, the two groups shared a fate, while Ibn Jarir identifies them as the same people and explains the omitted “brother” as brevity.
rows.anchor: أهل مدين عذبوا بعذاب الظلة فإن كانوا غير أصحاب الأيكة كما زعم مقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mukhsirīn are those who reduce measures or weights; akhsartu the measure means you made it deficient.
rows.anchor: من الناقصين للكيل يقال أخسرت الكيل والوزن إذا نقصته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas transmits that when asked which term Moses completed, the Prophet said he fulfilled the fuller and better one.
rows.anchor: روى ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه سئل أي الأجلين قضى موسى قال أوفاهما وأطيبهما

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says Moses stayed with the family for ten further years after completing the term.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد مكث بعد قضاء الأجل عندهم عشرا أخر

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih says Moses stayed there for years after bringing his wife into the household.
rows.anchor: وقال وهب بن منبه أقام عندهم بعد أن أدخل عليه امرأته سنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafiʿ, Abu ʿAmr, Ibn ʿAmir, and al-Kisaʾi read jidhwa with kasra; ʿAsim uses fatḥa; Hamza, Khalaf, and al-Walid from Ibn ʿAmir use ḍamma. All are dialect forms.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر والكسائي جذوة بكسر الجيم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says a jidhwa is a piece of wood with fire; Abu ʿUbayda calls it a thick piece of wood without flame, like the stump of a tree.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس الجذوة قطعة حطب فيها نار وقال أبو عبيدة قطعة غليظة من الحطب

rows.speaker: ابن مقبل
rows.claim: Ibn Muqbil’s poem uses jazl al-jadhā for substantial, sound firewood, supporting Abu ʿUbayda’s lexical explanation.
rows.anchor: باتت حواطب ليلى يلتمسن لها جزل الجذا غير خوار ولا دعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording through “or a brand” was already explained in the commentary on 20:10.
rows.anchor: وقد سبق تفسير هذه الآية طه إلى قوله ﴿ أو جذوة ﴾
